summary: Observation of a row of luminous rectangles with 2 flashes.
description: On Wednesday, December 9, 1992, around 9:00 PM, a gendarme, deputy to the brigade commander, and his wife observed a large-scale luminous phenomenon: five or six illuminated rectangles in a line, along with two particularly intense blue flashes, one at each end of the row of rectangles. The observation lasted only a few seconds. The driver braked, and the vehicle behind him also slowed down, but this second vehicle could not be located. The phenomenon could not be explained.

summary: Two stars likely to be seen under a winter sky
description: For several nights around December 23, 1992, a witness and his wife observed several very bright points of light with changing colors from their home. During one observation, he noted sudden changes in position. The investigation revealed that this was likely a case of mistaken identity with stars identified as Aldebaran and Gamma. The reported sudden changes in position could not be confirmed.

summary: Observation of a rapid green light
description: On November 21, 1992, at approximately 6:30 p.m., a witness in a car observed a green light moving very quickly. Despite the nearby airport, the witness believed it could not have been an aircraft. Although the witness was accompanied by their spouse, only one statement was recorded. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of an intense white light in a loud noise
description: On November 16, 1992, at approximately 4:30 a.m., a witness was awakened by a loud noise resembling a jet engine, accompanied by two flashes of light illuminating his bedroom. He then observed a large, very bright white ball of light. After about ten seconds, a nearby villa was illuminated in red, and with another noise, the white light disappeared. This villa, uninhabited at the time, sustained no damage. After the white light vanished, a red dot remained above a tree, and a light mist lingered where the white ball had been. Despite the reported noise, no other witnesses could be found. However, a neighbor, although he saw nothing, noticed around the same time that his dogs were very frightened. The observed phenomenon could not be identified.

summary: Observation of a red mass passing very close to a vehicle
description: On November 12, 1992, at approximately 5:00 PM, a witness driving a car was startled by a large, flashing red mass that rapidly approached the witness silently. The sighting lasted only a few seconds but the object passed within about 50 meters of the vehicle. The phenomenon could not be identified.

On October 21, 1992, at approximately 7:00 PM, a couple in a car observed a very rapid phenomenon lasting 2 to 3 seconds: a luminous sphere followed by a trail and incandescent points. Despite the limited information available, it seems likely that this couple witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Likely sighting of two helicopters at night
description: On October 18th, around 10:00 PM, a couple in a car observed first one, then two, stationary, flashing lights at a low altitude. The lights were orange with a white glow and rotated counterclockwise. A dark shape was located beneath the lights. After about ten minutes, the lights finally disappeared, moving very slowly. Although the sighting was silent, it is very likely that the witnesses saw the lights of two helicopters hovering in mid-air, which then flew away.

On October 11, 1992, between 9:30 and 10:30 PM, two independent witnesses observed a whitish, oval shape moving slowly over Marseille. Both witnesses took the precaution of filming their observation. The investigations by the two brigades quickly revealed that the witnesses had observed, from a distance, an airship based in Marignane and conducting promotional night flights. The flight data perfectly matched the witnesses' description.

summary: Observation of an intense light and a slowly moving oval phenomenon
description: On two occasions, on July 14, 1992, around 2:00 AM and again in early September around 11:00 PM, a witness observed a very bright white light for about a minute, the intensity of which varied slowly. Then, accompanied by his daughter, he observed a very bright, white, oval-shaped phenomenon for another minute, moving slowly and silently across the sky. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a white oval glow
description: On the night of August 24-25, 1992, around midnight, two young men on a moped observed a glow above the trees that "followed" them to the home of one of them. This glow was whitish, oval-shaped, and silent. The weather was mild and the sky clear. The two young men were very frightened, which prompted them to give a statement, but no further information could be obtained.

summary: Observation of a silent oval object and a human shape. Disappearance at high speed.
description: On August 3, 1992, around 1:00 AM, a motorist spotted a lenticular-shaped white haze above an embankment bordering a field. Located 10 meters from the vehicle and 3 meters above it, the haze dissipated, and the witness then saw a dark gray, oval-shaped object with a transparent upper section, revealing a human figure in a pilot's position, wearing a silver jumpsuit and helmet. The object made no sound. Waking his wife, who was in the back seat, she witnessed the same thing. Suddenly, beams of violet light appeared in front of and above the vehicle, frightening the witnesses. The driver decided to accelerate. His wife was the last to see a cylindrical object disappear at very high speed. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a red object shaped like a rugby ball
description: On July 3, 1992, at approximately 12:30 a.m., two 16-year-olds spotted a red, rugby ball-shaped object surrounded by flames. After hovering for a few seconds, the object plummeted rapidly to the ground. The following day, the teenagers went to the presumed crash site and found flattened areas with marks on the ground. The investigation attributed the flattened areas and marks to severe weather (several fields were in the same condition) but uncovered no further information about the phenomenon.

summary: Observation of the passage of a very rapid triangular shape
description: On May 26, 1992, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness and his mother observed a triangular shape with yellow lights at its apex. The object, which appeared metallic, moved very quickly, and the observation lasted only about three seconds.

summary: Observation of a very bright light during stormy weather
description: On May 23, 1992, around midnight, two witnesses in two different vehicles observed a very bright light for two to three seconds. The weather was stormy, but the witnesses were unable to identify the phenomenon as lightning.

summary: Observations of a fixed yellow light spot then changing shape and moving on an upward trajectory; change of direction and moving away: observation of an airplane.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named COULOMMIERS (77) 12.05.1992, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On May 12, 1992, at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness on the first floor of their home observed "a bright yellow spot" in the sky. Joined by a second witness (T2), they observed the UFO, which appeared to lengthen and slowly follow an upward trajectory. In a final phase, the UFO changed direction, leaving a yellow trail behind it. No noise was heard during the observation. The UFO gradually moved away. These two testimonies were recorded by the gendarmerie, which launched an investigation (see report). T1 reported at the beginning of the interview report two other observations made previously. The UFO observed by the two witnesses resembled a simple aircraft, initially seen head-on, with landing lights on, appearing stationary or moving slowly in the direction of the witnesses; Then, in a second and third phase, having made a turn while gaining altitude until encountering an atmospheric layer more conducive to the formation of a contrail, and appearing to move rapidly, accelerating abruptly after its turn, as observed more transversely (see the investigation report). This contrail probably even began to be visible at the end of the first phase, as it was very short, but since the witnesses could not distinguish the aircraft from its contrail, they initially mistook it for a single, elongating object, only to distinguish the two later, when the contrail lengthened further after the turn. This aircraft may have taken off in VFRn (night flight) from Auxerre-Branches airport and headed north, facing the witnesses, before making a turn to the northeast, towards its final destination. The appearance of the UFO described by the witnesses in phase 1 (a bright, yellow to very bright spot) is entirely consistent with this hypothesis, which they only reject due to the absence of any perceived noise. However, at a great distance and depending on the wind (tailwind or tailwind), the noise of an aircraft may very well not be perceived. In the second phase, the description given by the witnesses (a very long, luminous trail of the same color) fits perfectly with the observation of a condensation trail produced by this aircraft, which was at that moment at an altitude conducive to the formation of such a trail. Since the observation took place at dusk, we attempted to determine whether it was possible that this trail was still illuminated by the sun, which was already 10° below the horizon at the time of the observation. Unfortunately, too many uncertainties in the existing data and variables sensitive to measurements are present, preventing a definitive conclusion on this point. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of an aircraft.

summary: Observation for about twenty minutes of 3 bright points in a triangle: lack of information.
description: On April 25, 1992, at approximately 7:30 a.m., a witness observed three bright points of light forming a triangle in the sky. The group appeared to be a large object rotating slowly on its axis. The observation lasted about twenty minutes. No further information was gathered.

On March 1, 1992, at approximately 3:30 a.m., a witness and about ten guests saw a luminous mass moving slowly across the sky with a trail of various colors. None of the guests present were interviewed. At the same time, in the same department, other witnesses in cars observed a similar phenomenon lasting 30 to 40 seconds. Each of the accounts is rather brief, but taken together, they suggest that it was an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation for about fifteen seconds of a brown oval shape
description: On February 10, 1992, at approximately 7:30 a.m., a single witness in a car observed a stationary, brown and orange oval shape, about the size of a helicopter. The observation lasted approximately 15 seconds. No information could be gathered to confirm or explain this sighting.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation without a precise date of the passage of two luminous triangles: lack of information.
description: In April 2008, a witness reported an observation that occurred in the summer of 1992. Since the witness could not recall the date, the case was arbitrarily dated July 1, 1992. Around midnight, at a place called Le Mirador in Cap-Ferret, two people observed the slow, silent, and low-altitude passage of two overlapping triangles, illuminated at their extremities by a white light. The phenomenon abruptly ceased. This account of a strange observation does not mention a precise date. Therefore, an investigation is impossible. This case is classified as "C" due to the lack of a precise date.
